title: Dynamic seqlen-aware SwarmBench for heterogeneous TP/PP throughput profiling
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Build a reproducible, automated benchmark harness (SwarmBench) that measures tokens/sec and tail latency across tensor-parallel (TP) and pipeline-parallel (PP) multi-GPU topologies with realistic, dynamic sequence-length mixes and heterogeneous GPU types. The harness must model production traffic (short+long prompt cohorts, KV cache warmup patterns, microbursts) and produce artifacts suitable for automated regression detection and CI gating. This ticket covers design, prototype harness, baseline runs, and integration with Grafana and regression alerts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run TP-only, PP-only, and TP+PP topologies across 2-16 GPUs and heterogeneous GPU mixes.
2) Can replay configured seqlen distributions (cohorts) and microburst profiles; results reproducible within 5% across repeated runs after warmup.
3) Outputs time-series and per-run summary artifacts (CSV, JSON), baseline reference, and Grafana dashboards.
4) Automated regression detector flags >5% drop in tokens/sec or p95 regressions with at most 1% false positive rate on historical baseline.
5) CI gating hook (PR/merge blocker) implemented to fail when a statistically significant regression is detected vs baseline.
test_plan:
- Workloads: create three canonical seqlen cohorts (chat-short: 8-32 tokens, interactive: 64-256, long-form: 512-2048) and mix ratios to simulate product tiers.
- Warmup: enforce KV cache priming runs and measure warmup plateau; exclude first N seconds from steady-state metrics.
- Topologies: test TP-only (all-replica), PP-only (staged), and TP+PP hybrid with degree sweep.
- Heterogeneity: run mixes with A100+H100 and mixed memory/compute older GPUs to capture scheduling impact.
- Microbursts: inject Poisson burst patterns and fixed microburst windows to test transient p95 spikes.
- Measurement: sliding 60s steady-state windows after warmup; report tokens/sec, p95/p99, and variance.
- Reproducibility: run 5 repeats per config and store results to gs://redwood-bench-results/swarmbench/<run-id>.
- Tooling: use existing load-gen with sequence-length sampler, and instrument with tracing hooks to correlate token emission to kernel-level metrics.
regression_detection:
- Baseline: compute a rolling baseline using median tokens/sec and median p95 over the last 30 successful runs for a given topology+model+seqlen-mix.
- Tests: bootstrap confidence intervals on medians, complemented by Welch's t-test on log-transformed tokens/sec when distribution is near-normal after transform.
- Control charts: CUSUM + EWMA for low-latency detection of small drifts; Shewhart rule for large step regressions.
- Thresholds: flag if tokens/sec drops by >5% beyond 95% bootstrap CI OR p95 increases by >15% with p-value < 0.01.
- CI Integration: regression detector runs as post-step on nightly and PR runs; failures annotate PR with summary + link to diff heatmap and link to detailed artifacts.
- Mitigation: automated rollback suggestion to previous pinned runtime variant and create ENG ticket with diagnostics bundle if regression persists.
updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed comparing fixed-seqlen vs dynamic-seqlen mixes. Observed 12% lower tokens/sec when median seqlen >512 on mixed TP/PP for older GPU shapes. Added heterogeneity to scope.

2026-02-22: Prototype harness (load-gen + seqlen-sampler) merged to feature branch. Initial runs show high p95 variance during first 90s due to KV warmup; adjusted warmup policy to 3x median context windows.

2026-03-01: Early baseline collected for small topology (4xA100 TP-only) with three seqlen cohorts. Stored artifacts and dashboard panels for tokens/sec, p95, and CUSUM. Shared with runtime team for review.
2026-03-05: Regression detection design reviewed with SRE and Applied ML. Agreed on bootstrap medians + EWMA for drift sensitivity. Action: implement CI hook and PR annotation format.

2026-03-09: Heterogeneous run (2xA100 + 2xH100 TP+PP hybrid) completed. Found a scheduling inefficiency causing 7% tokens/sec drop when older GPUs host KV-heavy stages. Created follow-up ENG ticket ENG-88322 (scheduling-kernel-pin) and marked as dependency.
2026-03-10: Demo to PM + Console team. Requested Grafana panel changes to include per-cohort tokens/sec breakdown and exportable CSV for release notes. Added 'export-csv' task to next steps.
next_steps:
1) Finish CUSUM/EWMA implementation and schedule nightly runs against baseline.
2) Add CI gating hook that annotates PRs with a compact regression summary and links to artifacts.
3) Run full sweep across 2/4/8/16 GPU configs with mixed seqlen mixes and store canonical baselines.
4) Work with runtime team (follow-up ENG ticket ENG-88322) to investigate scheduler variance on heterogeneous GPU runs.
5) Add exportable CSV panel and automated release-note snippet generator for cross-team consumption.
notes: This harness is intentionally named SwarmBench to emphasize many-worker, mixed-cohort workloads. Focus on creating deterministic post-processed artifacts so downstream teams (console, optimize) can consume stable signals for cost/latency tradeoff recommendations.
